ordered_diagnoses: dermal lymphatic invasion by breast cancer

s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive subcutaneous node in the axilla with skin infiltration and episodic pain
salient_findings: Slowly growing subcutaneous node in the right axilla
Progressive infiltration of the overlying skin
Erythematous plaque in the right axilla measuring 5 × 3 cm
Dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement
Tumor cells with basophilic nuclei and scant cytoplasm in an 'Indian file pattern'
Positive immunohistochemistry for pancytokeratin, cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3
key_facts: Woman in her 60s
Subcutaneous node in the right axilla first noticed 10 years ago
Progressive infiltration of the overlying skin over the past year
Swelling in the right axilla during pregnancy over 20 years ago
Mild episodic pain in the right axilla during menstrual cycles
Solitary, indolent, erythematous plaque in the right axilla measuring 5 × 3 cm
Dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement
Tumor cells diffusely dispersed between collagen bundles
Tumor cells with basophilic nuclei and scant cytoplasm
Positive immunohistochemistry for pancytokeratin, cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3
Negative immunohistochemistry for synaptophysin, chromogranin, and S100
Multiple GATA3-positive and estrogen receptor–positive apocrine glands in close association to diffuse tumor cell infiltration
1 of the sentinel lymph nodes showed isolated cytokeratin8/18–positive tumor cells and MNF116-positive tumor cells
No evidence of primary or secondary tumors on chest, abdominal, and pelvic CT scans, cranial and breast MRI, mammography, and breast sonography

shortlist: dermal lymphatic invasion by breast cancer

raw.rationale: The presence of GATA3-positive and estrogen receptor–positive apocrine glands in close association with diffuse tumor cell infiltration, along with positive immunohistochemistry for pancytokeratin, cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3, strongly supports the diagnosis of apocrine carcinoma.

rejected.label: hidradenocarcinoma
rejected.why: While hidradenocarcinoma is a type of sweat gland carcinoma, the specific immunohistochemical profile and association with apocrine glands points more towards apocrine carcinoma.

rejected.label: dermal lymphatic invasion by breast cancer
rejected.why: The lack of evidence of primary or secondary breast tumors on imaging studies makes this option less likely.

rejected.label: sweat gland carcinoma
rejected.why: This is a broader category that includes apocrine carcinoma, but the specific features of the case make apocrine carcinoma a more precise diagnosis.

rejected.label: apocrine gland carcinoma
rejected.why: This option is essentially synonymous with apocrine carcinoma, but 'apocrine carcinoma' is the preferred term used in the context of the provided information.
